title: Jay-Z Will Finally Perform at the Super Bowl Halftime Show
summary:
Rapper Jay-Z will take the Super Bowl halftime stage in February, the NFL has announced. It will be his first time performing at the championship game, even though his company, Roc Nation, has produced the halftime show since 2019 and he has helped pick each year's performer.

Super Bowl LXI will take place on February 14 near Los Angeles. Jay-Z will follow recent halftime stars including Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd. The show draws global attention, while tens of millions of people in the United States watch the game.

Kendrick Lamar's 2025 performance was the most watched Super Bowl halftime show in history and won the Emmy award for outstanding music direction. The announcement came after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, performed two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played, as part of a tour celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt.

From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey, Jay-Z said. Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact Jay-Z will bring.

Goodell added that when the NFL first agreed with Roc Nation to produce the show, he had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. Jay-Z's honors include being the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, 25 Grammy awards, and induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.
why_it_matters: It shows how a long music career can lead to one of the world's biggest stages, and how the artists behind a show can finally step into the spotlight themselves.
